1.text: Comets are called “smoking-stars” by the Chukchee. The word “smoke”

2.text: indicates that they suppose much cooking is being done there. Planets are

3.text: called “crooked-way stars,” because of their irregular path. Among these,

4.text: Venus has a separate name, Hɪtoˊ-ʟap. The first part of this name means
4.resolved: Hɪtoˊ-ʟap = H, I=U+026A, t, o, U+02CA, -, L=U+029F, a, p

5.text: “large,” “extensive.” The Chukchee could not explain the second root of

6.text: this name; but probably it agrees with the Koryak word Lêlaˊpɪčan (“star”),
6.resolved: Lêlaˊpɪčan = L, e+U+0302, l, a, U+02CA, p, I=U+026A, c+U+030C, a, n

7.text: which, in its turn, is derived from the verb lêlaˊpekin (“to look on”), and
7.resolved: lêlaˊpekin = l, e+U+0302, l, a, U+02CA, p, e, k, i, n (plain i, not small-cap)

8.text: means literally “one looking on.” The Chukchee name of Venus, therefore,

9.text: means “large star.” Venus, when the morning-star, is also called Kêrg-

10.text: añaˊʟɪñɪn (“bright star”). The Chukchee say that Venus is mŭk-äviˊrɪnleᵋn
10.resolved: añaˊʟɪñɪn = a, n+U+0303, a, U+02CA, L=U+029F, I=U+026A, n+U+0303, I=U+026A, n; mŭk = m, u+U+0306, k; äviˊrɪnleᵋn = a+U+0308, v, i, U+02CA, r, I=U+026A, n, l, e, U+1D4B, n

11.text: (“with many clothes”), because she shines with changing colors. Shooting-

12.text: stars are said to be stars that go coasting down hill on sleds. The Koryak

13.text: suppose that they take alms to the needy in heaven. Those that shoot away

14.text: from land toward the sea carry reindeer-meat, while those that move in an

15.text: opposite direction carry whale-blubber. The Asiatic Eskimo say of shooting-

16.text: stars, that they have diarrhœa.¹ When there is an eclipse of the moon, the

17.text: Chukchee say that a keˊlᴇ wants to swallow the moon.
17.resolved: keˊlᴇ = k, e, U+02CA, l, E=U+1D07 (small-cap, obscure-vowel series). Mark here can only be stress (l is not in the spirant post-consonant list nor is the environment V_V), so unambiguous.

19.resolved: vaˊɪrgɪt = v, a, [mark], I=U+026A, r, g, I=U+026A, t. Mark is V_V (a_ɪ) — the one residual shape judgement (§2.1/§4): shape here is indistinguishable to me from the page's unambiguous stress marks (cf. line 4, 17), so keyed as U+02CA (stress). Flag for human shape check — same ambiguity recurs on lines 20, 21, 22 (x2) for this same word ’vaˊɪrgɪn/-t’, and on line 42 for ’erkɪn’.

23.text: are but little more than names. These names may replace one another.

24.text: The first name is used chiefly in cosmogonical tales; the second, and more

25.text: particularly the third, in prayers and incantations.

26.text: All of these “Beings” are powerful, and just and benevolent toward man.

27.text: They represent a very loose and indefinite personification of the creative

28.text: principle of the world, and are similar to Great Manitou or to Wakanda of

29.text: the Indians, which are quite as indefinite in meaning. The Zenith, the Mid-

30.text: day, the Dawn, are also often considered identical with the Creator of the

31.text: world. With those who have been baptized, the Christian God, under the

32.text: name of Eˊñeñ,³ has taken a place side by side with these vague superior
32.resolved: Eˊñeñ = E (plain ASCII capital), U+02CA (stress, non-V_V: E_ñ), n+U+0303, e, n+U+0303

33.text: beings. The Chukchee, however, point out that the Creator does not belong

34.text: to those sacrificed to. They say there is no need to sacrifice to the Creator.

35.text: Upper Being, Merciful Being, Life-giving Being, Luck-giving Being, may receive

36.text: sacrifices, though these sacrifices are not included in the yearly cycle of cere-

37.text: monials. More often sacrifices to Dawn, Zenith, and Mid-day are at the same

38.text: time offered to the benevolent “Beings” mentioned before.

39.text: ¹ Nelson (p. 449) says that the shooting-stars are termed “star-dung” by the Alaskan Eskimo.
